forecast-period.text: A trough located near the northern border of SA will shift north over the next few days as a high pressure system moves across the south. The high will move into the Tasman Sea later on Thursday with a trough moving into the far west on Friday before weakening over the weekend.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Chance of isolated light morning showers about the southern agricultural area. Showers and thunderstorms about the pastoral districts. Maximum temperatures below to well below average. Southwest to southeasterly winds, fresh at times in the northeast.

Showers and isolated thunderstorms about the pastoral districts, easing during the evening. Mostly dry elsewhere. Maximum temperatures below to well below average. East to southeasterly winds, fresh at times about the west coast and in the northeast.

Mostly dry, with isolated showers and thunderstorms developing in the far west during the afternoon. Maximum temperatures near average in the west, grading to below average in the northeast. Southeast to northeasterly winds.

text.p: Showers and thunderstorms in the west, extending to the far north during the afternoon. Isolated showers about the southeast. Maximum temperatures near to above average in the south, gradient to below average in the north. East to northeasterly winds, tending east to southeasterly in the far west.
Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Friday: Broadly 5 to 10 mm across the pastoral districts, increasing 20 to 40 mm in the far north. Less than 2 mm across the south.
